gaps.sentence: Let me ___ a look at that cut on your arm.
gaps.explanation: take a look (at something) is the fixed collocation for examining something briefly.

gaps.sentence: Most children learn to ___ the time before they start school.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the time (read a clock)
gaps.explanation: tell the time means to be able to read a clock; it is a fixed expression.

gaps.sentence: We stopped at a cafe to ___ a chat.
gaps.explanation: have a chat is the fixed collocation for a friendly, informal conversation.

gaps.sentence: Why don't we ___ lunch together on Friday?
gaps.explanation: have lunch is the standard collocation for eating lunch.

gaps.sentence: There was ___ fog at the airport all morning.
gaps.explanation: thick fog (or dense fog) is the standard collocation; 'strong fog' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: I ___ a strange dream last night.
gaps.explanation: have a dream is the English collocation; 'see a dream' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: The roads were almost empty — the traffic was surprisingly ___.
gaps.explanation: light traffic means few vehicles on the road; its opposite is heavy traffic.

gaps.sentence: He didn't ___ any interest in politics until university.
gaps.explanation: take an interest in something means to become curious or involved in it.
